subject: MB GOF Test - Removal of single sites appruptly changes ModelFit

messages.author: a284bd5d34acd859
messages.subject: MB GOF Test - Removal of single sites appruptly changes ModelFit
parts:
Dear all! 

I am dealing with some uncertainty concerning the evaluation of my Single Species Occupancy Models. I used different Test, Freeman Tukey e.g., but also MacKenzie Bailey Goodness of Fit as implemented in AICcmodavg. 

My research concentrates on ungulates in a mainly forested area.

I tested many different parameters for psi and selected models via dredge. I evaluated the global model and also checked the selected top model for model-fit using MB gof test. 

For some cases I got very "difficult" results. p-values of zero, high c-hat values (>30, in some cases really astromically high). After closer examination of the chisqu-table, I realized, that the model for most sites did quite a good job, but for single sites (1-3 out of >100) the chisq values were extremly and extraordinary high. Those were sites where nearly every occasion showed site usage ("1") and only one site would build the whole cohorte . Removing those sites improved my model fit, the same variables were selected anyway, and the models passed the gof test. 

What is your opinion? Is this way of dealing with this problematic? 



thank you very much

Maresa

parts:
Dear Maresa,

 

OK, thanks. So, you don’t have minute sample sizes. I had the hypothesis that when you have, say, 8 sites, then dropping one atypical one may make a big difference.

 

If you can make a good point for dropping out some or all of these atypical sites, then perhaps that would be a solution. However, outliers sometimes provide valuable opportunities for learning about a system.

Best regards  -- Marc
